tools.name: ui_get_tree
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: ui.get_tree] Returns the visible UMG widget tree as JSON - a text substitute for looking at a screenshot. Prefer scoping it: 'ui.get_tree GameOption' returns only that window and is far smaller than the whole screen. 'top' selects the top-most window, which is what you usually want right after a popup appears. Without --window the entire screen is returned, grouped by UI layer. Layout-only containers (CanvasPanel, Overlay, SizeBox, boxes) are folded away and their children lifted, label text is absorbed into the button/tab that owns it, collapsed or unpainted or off-screen subtrees are dropped, and more than 12 identical siblings collapse into a {role:'more', count:N} entry. Only interactive nodes get a 'ref' and a 'rect' - everything else is there to be read, not clicked. Scroll containers report offset/max/pos, and list views additionally report the total item count plus the index range that currently has entry widgets (items outside that range are virtualized away and have no widget at all, so you must scroll to reach them). When the max_nodes budget is hit the response carries a 'truncated' field - it never drops nodes silently. Fails if --window matches no visible window. This command never creates a widget, so it is safe to poll; widgets opened this very frame appear one poll later.

tools.name: ui_list_windows
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: ui.list_windows] Lists the top-level UMG windows currently on screen, without any of their contents. This is the cheapest UI query and the intended first step: pick a window here, then call ui.get_tree --window=<name> to see inside it. Windows are ordered top-most first (by UI layer z-order). Each entry carries 'counts' (nodes / interactive / scrollables) so you can tell how big the window's tree is before asking for it, and 'occluded' which is true when a modal above it means clicks cannot reach it. Only windows under the UI manager's root widget are reported; Cohtml-based UI and world-space widget components are not UMG and never appear. Returns an empty list when there is no world. This command never creates a widget, so it is safe to poll. Widgets that were opened this very frame have not been painted yet and show up one poll later.

tools.name: ui_scroll
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: ui.scroll] Scrolls a scroll box or list view identified by a ref from ui.get_tree. By default it calls the scroll API directly, which lands on the target in one step and makes the result easy to verify; the response carries the resulting offset/max/pos/at_end so you do not have to re-query. For a scroll box the offset is in slate units; for a list view it is in items. Fails when there is no world or the ref is not scrollable.

tools.name: ui_click
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: ui.click] Clicks a UMG widget identified by a ref from ui.get_tree / ui.find. By default this synthesizes real mouse input at the widget's centre - it moves the cursor there, presses, and sends the RELEASE ON A LATER TICK, because the engine does not treat a press and release delivered in the same tick as a click. That means the click has NOT completed when this command returns: re-query ui.get_tree / ui.list_windows to see the result. Use hold_ticks if one tick is not enough. Because it goes through the real input path, hit testing, modality and input blocking all apply exactly as they do for a player - if something covers the widget the call FAILS instead of clicking. The Slate application is activated first, so this works with the game window in the background. force=true skips input synthesis entirely and invokes the widget's click delegate directly (buttons only), which bypasses hit testing and input blocking and can drive the game into a state a player cannot reach - it is synchronous, so unlike the default path the effect has already happened when the command returns. 'method' always reports which path ran (synth_input or delegate). Dimmed, disabled and non-hit-testable widgets are rejected outright. For a list entry, note the ref is only valid until the list scrolls - entry widgets are recycled, so scroll first (ui.scroll --to=index), re-query, then click. Passing x and y instead of ref clicks a raw viewport position; nothing verifies what it lands on, so prefer a ref. Fails when there is no world.

tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: camera.get_view] Returns the live state of the active game camera: world position, rotation, the forward/right/up unit vectors derived from that rotation, the field of view actually in effect this frame, aspect ratio, projection mode, viewport resolution, the current inZOI camera mode (ShoulderView, QuarterView, BuildView, PhotoMode, ...) and the actor the camera is following. This reads the camera cache the renderer used, so fov here is the value in effect right now, which can differ from the user preference reported by camera.get_settings. aspect_ratio is the effective one used to render (the viewport aspect unless the camera constrains it), not the camera's raw AspectRatio field, which normally sits at an unused 4:3 default. Coordinates are Unreal world space: left-handed, Z-up, centimetres, with forward = +X, right = +Y, up = +Z. The camera interpolates and does collision avoidance every frame, so treat the result as a snapshot; pause the simulation first if you need a stable reading.

tools.name: ui_dismiss
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: ui.dismiss] Closes the top-most blocking UI, up to max_steps elements in one call. Priority: coach mark -> cat talk -> popup -> ESC stack -> cutscene. For a popup it clicks the CANCEL button, never the action button: with two or more buttons it only clicks a non-dimmed Secondary/SecondaryNegative button and only when exactly one exists; a single-button popup is treated as an acknowledgement and is clicked. Clicking runs that button's bound script and delegate for real. Popup enumeration order is UObject creation order, NOT z-order, so the popup acted on is a best guess. Destructive confirmations (quit game, leave to lobby, delete, overwrite, discard, reset - matched as whole words, so 'Preset' is not read as 'Reset') are additionally on a deny-list and are NEVER auto-clicked; neither are popups with an empty popup_id, which are opened directly by a handler and cannot be verified as safe. A popup is closed outright (without clicking) only when its widget tree contains no button at all, so a popup that shows buttons never loses its decision delegates. When a popup is left untouched the call fails with stop_reason 'blocked_by:<popup_id> ...' (decide yourself and use ui.click_popup_button) or 'stuck:<popup_id> - all buttons dimmed' (nothing can be clicked at all). Loading screens are NEVER dismissed - poll ui.get_blocking and wait them out. Fails when there is no world. Safe to call repeatedly; within one call a target is never attempted twice.

tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: game.exit_map_view] Closes the world map overview and descends the camera into the current site, which is what actually opens the HUD and starts play. Success is verified after the fact (the map pawn's transition flag must have gone down), so a close request that the pawn silently ignored is reported as a failure instead of a bogus accept. tools.name: game_list_saves
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: game.list_saves] Returns save slots sorted by saved_time descending (newest first), one page at a time. Feed 'folder' (and 'file' when it differs) into game.load. The cached slot order is NOT trusted; the list is re-sorted by saved_time here. PAGED: only 'limit' entries (20 by default) are returned starting at 'offset'. A profile can hold hundreds of slots, so an unbounded dump would be tens of kilobytes per call. Because the payload is a bare array there is nowhere to put paging metadata inside it, so the total count, the offset and the next offset are reported in the result MESSAGE, e.g. '20 of 366 save slot(s) (offset 0, limit 20). More available: pass offset=20 for the next page.' By default this reads the already-scanned slot list and does no disk IO. Pass refresh=true only when the save directory changed underneath the client - a rescan reads a thumbnail file per slot, rebuilds every slot object (invalidating the cache the load-list UI holds) and deletes incomplete fork directories. Higher-version saves are listed (see is_higher_version); loading one opens a fork-warning popup that ui.dismiss refuses to touch, so clear it with ui.click_popup_button.

tools.name: building_construct_room
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: building.construct_room] [Build Mode Only] Builds all four walls of an axis-aligned rectangular room in ONE command and ONE undo step. PREFER THIS over four building.construct_wall calls, especially above floor_level 0. Building a room side by side does not work on upper floors: the engine resets the elevation of any room that is not closed yet, so the 2nd and 4th side silently fail to attach and you end up with 2 of 4 walls. This command runs all four sides inside one root command, so the room is already closed when that check runs. x0/y0 and x1/y1 are OPPOSITE CORNERS in centimetres, site-relative with the origin at the site's MINIMUM CORNER - the same space as build.scan_walls and building.place_object. Order does not matter; each side must be at least 50cm. Endpoints snap to the 25cm grid, so the resulting wall centre lines land on 25*k+12.5. HEIGHTS: for floor_level above 0 the storey elevation goes into 'floor_height', NOT 'base_height' - the engine resets base_height to 0, so a room built that way silently lands at ground level. Just omit floor_height and it is derived from the top of the floor below. Heights are also inherited from a wall graph the rectangle touches. wall_height defaults to 300cm (3.0m). SUCCESS IS VERIFIED: 'sides_created' and 'sides' are read back from the wall graph afterwards, and 'result_*_height' reports what the graph actually kept. Anything less than 4 sides fails loudly. Walls are free - nothing is charged. Requires phase == 'ready' (see build.get_mode_state).

tools.name: building_construct_wall
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: building.construct_wall] [Build Mode Only] Builds a SINGLE wall segment between two site-relative points on the given floor. To build a whole rectangular room use building.construct_room instead - it is one undo step and it is the ONLY reliable way above floor_level 0, because the engine resets the elevation of a room that is not closed yet and the sides you add later then fail to attach. COORDINATES are in centimetres with the origin (0,0) at the site's MINIMUM CORNER, and the usable range is 0..site_size - call build.get_site_info and read 'coord_space' first. Do NOT use 'site_half_extent' as the full size; it is half, and using it confines the build to one quadrant. Endpoints snap to a 25cm grid. Goes through the build undo/redo stack (revert with building.undo). Wall construction is NOT charged to the household wallet - walls are free by game policy, unlike objects placed with building.place_object. Set is_delete=true to remove the segment instead. HEIGHTS: the storey elevation for floor_level above 0 lives in 'floor_height', NOT 'base_height' - the engine resets base_height to 0 on any room that is not closed yet, so anything you put there is thrown away and the wall lands at ground level. Omit floor_height and it is derived from the top of the floor below. When the new segment touches an existing wall, all three heights are inherited from that wall's graph instead, exactly as the in-game ghost wall does. The values actually used come back as applied_base_height / applied_floor_height / applied_wall_height, and wall_height defaults to 300cm (3.0m). SUCCESS IS VERIFIED against the wall graph after the fact: 'wall_created' and 'segment_wall_count' report whether a wall really exists in the requested span, so a rejected wall fails loudly instead of returning committed=true with nothing built. Requires phase == 'ready' (see build.get_mode_state). Partial failure of nested sub-commands is not detectable; verify the result with build.scan_walls.

tools.name: building_place_object
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: building.place_object] [Build Mode Only] Places a NEW object from the Object data table onto the current site, through the build undo/redo stack (revert with building.undo). Call build.get_site_info first and read its 'build_rules' - it states the coordinate space, the rotation space and the wall auto-alignment this command assumes. This is the only way to add furniture to an empty site - building.move_object / copy_object / put_in_inventory all require an existing entity_id. Find valid ids with data.list_rows --alias=Object, and inspect one (display name, category, price, asset) with data.table_get --alias=Object --row=<id>. COORDINATES are in centimetres with the origin (0,0) at the site's MINIMUM CORNER; the usable range is 0..site_size from build.get_site_info 'coord_space'. Do NOT use 'site_half_extent' as the full size. SLOT SNAPPING (snap=true, default): after placing, the object is attached to a free compatible slot of an OVERLAPPING object, using the same engine path as the in-game magnet. This is how a dining chair becomes a table chair - without it the chair is only a standalone seat and 'eat together at the table' interactions never appear. Detection is by COLLISION OVERLAP, not by radius: place the chair so its box actually touches the table, then check 'snapped' in the response. When it snaps, the slot decides the final position and rotation, so 'yaw' is overridden - and so are applied_x/applied_y/applied_z, which report the position REQUESTED of the engine, not where the slot ended up putting the object. Whenever 'snapped' is true, read the real final transform back with build.scan_objects. YAW IS SITE-RELATIVE, like x and y. Sites are rotated against the world (one measured at 174.5 degrees), and everything you can query - walls, rooms, floors - lives in site space, so yaw=0 means 'parallel to the site axes', not 'parallel to the world axes'. The response reports both applied_yaw (site) and applied_world_yaw. Which way the object visually faces also depends on how its mesh is authored - measured on Chair03, yaw=0 seats face -Y (the backrest faces +Y). Prefer snapping over hand-computed yaw for slotted furniture. DOORS AND WINDOWS are aligned for you: give any x/y NEAR the wall and the command snaps the object onto that wall's centre line, turns it to lie ALONG the wall (the only two valid facings differ by 180 degrees, which is what 'flip' picks between), and cuts the opening. This is required, not a convenience - the engine only cuts an opening when the object sits within 0.1cm of the wall centre line, which is at 25*k+12.5cm, so hand-picked round coordinates never work. Use 'flip' to choose which of the two valid facings it takes, and 'max_wall_distance' to widen or tighten the search. If no wall is close enough the call FAILS instead of leaving a door floating in mid-air; pass allow_free_place=true to override that. When you omit 'z', a door is put on the wall bottom and a window at a 90cm sill. Check 'wall_aligned', 'wall_edge_key', 'wall_opening' and 'applied_yaw' in the response. STAIRS AND LADDERS are quantised to 90 degrees, because their floor/ceiling hole is cut on an axis-aligned grid and a diagonal placement would gouge a much larger hole than the object. The value actually used comes back as 'applied_yaw'. Note that this command does NOT reproduce the in-game ghost preview's stair fitting (AB1BuildModeStairs), so the stairs keep their default rise: place them where the upper floor is one storey up. The object's price is charged to the household wallet and refunded by building.undo. Requires phase == 'ready' (see build.get_mode_state).

tools.name: screenshot_capture
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: screenshot.capture] Requests an engine screenshot and returns the exact absolute path, directory and filename the engine will write to. The path is authoritative, not a guess: the engine resolves the final filename at request time. OFFSCREEN-SAFE: this is a GPU read-back of the game's own render target, not a desktop grab, so it works while the game window is fully covered by other windows, unfocused, or moved off-screen — you do not need to bring the game to the foreground. SLOW AND DELAYED: nothing is on disk when this command returns. The file is only written when the engine renders and presents its next frame, so expect at least one frame of latency, and much longer (seconds) while a loading screen is up, while the window is minimised, or when the game thread is blocked by a map load. Poll screenshot.get_last until saved == true before reading the file. Only one request can be pending engine-wide; this fails if one is already in flight, or if Photo Mode currently owns the capture delegate (in that case the engine would write no file at all). Call system.get_paths for the directory these files land in.

tools.name: smartbuild_pick_surface_at_screen
tools.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] [CLI: smartbuild.pick_surface_at_screen] Ray-cast from a screen pixel and return what is under it. Drills through trees/foliage/blocking volumes using manual multi-step tracing on Visibility then GameObject channels. Target priority (first match wins): character > game object > wall/floor/ceiling. Used by drag-and-drop and other tools that need a surface or clothed body part under a cursor. Returns JSON with target="character"|"object"|"wall"|"floor"|"ceiling"|"none" and per-target fields: character={entity_id,bone,garment_type}, object={entity_id,part_index}, wall={floor_level,edge_key,side}, floor/ceiling={floor_level,room_index,is_ceil}. garment_type is auto-resolved from the hit bone and the character's equipped outfit (outer-first: hat>scarf, gloves>top, shoes>socks, etc.). On miss, reason is set and debug fields (hit_actor/hit_component/channel/step) are included. If x/y are omitted, the current mouse viewport position is used. Works in both play mode and build mode.

tools.name: data_patch
tools.description:
[CLI: data.patch] Apply an in-place data patch at runtime. Reverted on unmodding.
QUERY SYNTAX (STRICT):
  Every bracket selector MUST be Key=Value. Bare-value selectors like Table[Foo] or arr[0] will FAIL to parse.
    OK:   HouseholdBizConfig[Id=Default].baseEmployeeWagePerHour
    OK:   HouseholdBizConfig[Id=Default].householdBizSkillLevelInfo[level=0].baseEmployeeWagePerHour
    OK:   ItemTable[*].price            (wildcard over all rows)
    BAD:  HouseholdBizConfig[Default].baseEmployeeWagePerHour
    BAD:  householdBizSkillLevelInfo[0].baseEmployeeWagePerHour
COMMON KEYS:
  Top-level row Id is usually 'Id'. Inner arrays use their own key field (e.g. 'level', 'index', 'tier'). If unsure,
  fetch the row first via data.table_get and look at which scalar field uniquely identifies each array element.
METHODS:
  Override = replace the value at the path. Append/Insert = list operations.
VALIDATION (STRICT):
  The value is validated against the target schema BEFORE applying. A non-existent field name or a
  disallowed enum value FAILS with a specific reason (including the list of valid fields / enum values),
  instead of silently succeeding without any effect.
POST-PROCESS (OnPostJsonDataLoad):
  Append/Insert (single-row) auto-runs OnPostJsonDataLoad on the new row to populate derived fields
  (e.g. Object.ObjectTags merged from ObjectTemplate). Override/Wildcard does NOT auto-run because
  re-invoking it on already-processed rows can double-apply non-idempotent merges (e.g. Tags.Append).
  Pass refresh=true to force OnPostJsonDataLoad on every applied row regardless of method (use sparingly).

tools.name: motion_list
tools.description:
[CLI: motion.list] List CharacterAnim DataTable row IDs that can be played on a Zoi. 
IMPORTANT -- filter is effectively REQUIRED: the table holds thousands of rows. Calling motion.list without filter returns a truncated, low-signal sample that wastes tokens. ALWAYS infer a filter keyword from the user's natural-language request and pass filter=<keyword>. Examples of inference (do this BEFORE calling -- do not call without filter then re-call):
  'Make my Zoi dance / show dance motions / 춤추는 모션'      -> filter=dance
  'Do some yoga / stretching motions / 요가 동작'             -> filter=yoga
  'Sit down motions / 앉는 모션'                              -> filter=sit
  'Sleep / lie down / 자는 모션 / 눕는 모션'                  -> filter=sleep   (also try: lie, bed)
  'Walk / run / move / 걷는 / 달리는'                         -> filter=walk    (or run)
  'Cry / sad motion / 우는 모션'                              -> filter=cry
  'Laugh / happy motion / 웃는 모션'                          -> filter=laugh
  'Wave hand / greet / say hi / 인사하는 / 손 흔드는'         -> filter=wave    (or greet, hi, hello)
  'Hug / kiss / romantic / 포옹 / 키스'                       -> filter=hug     (or kiss)
  'Eat / drink / 먹는 / 마시는'                               -> filter=eat     (or drink)
  'Angry / fight / 화내는 / 싸우는'                           -> filter=angry   (or fight)
  'Random / 아무 모션 / 뭐든'                                 -> use motion.play_random instead
Only omit filter when the user EXPLICITLY asks 'show me all motions' / '전체 목록 / 전부 / 모든 모션' and is aware the result will be truncated. In that case prefer max=<small N> (e.g. 30) and warn the user.

validate=true: only return motions playable by the target character's gender/age/posture. Recommended whenever you plan to call motion.play right after, to avoid 'no valid montage' failures. max=<N>: limit results (default 50, max 500). Smaller is cheaper -- use 20~50 for chat answers.

Use the returned anim_id values with motion.play.

tools.name: uimod_scaffold
tools.description:
Create a UI mod or add a new app to an existing UI mod under the user InGame mods directory. TWO MODES:
  (A) NEW MOD: pass mod_name (and optionally app_name). mod_id is auto-generated as {mod_name}_{RANDOM6}. Creates {mod_id}.uplugin, mod_manifest.json, ui/uimod_apps.json, ui/{app_name}/uimod_manifest.json+index.html+app.js+window.js.
  (B) ADD APP TO EXISTING MOD: pass mod_id (must already exist under InGame/) and app_name. ONLY the new ui/{app_name}/ folder is created; the existing .uplugin / mod_manifest.json are kept intact (FriendlyName preserved). uimod_apps.json and mod_manifest.json NonAssets are auto-regenerated to include all apps. Use uimod.remount to hot-reload after.
IMPORTANT: BEFORE calling this tool, decide whether the new UI belongs in an existing multi-app mod or in a brand-new mod, and ASK the user explicitly. Use uimod_list to enumerate existing parent mods first. Each standalone mod has to be installed/distributed separately, so packing related apps under one mod is preferable.
Default trigger is 'game_mode' with the 'gameplay' alias (TopView/ShoulderView/ActiveMode/DiveView/Vehicle), so the mod is visible during normal play and auto-hides in Build / Character Studio / Photo / FreeCamera / Map / lobby menus. Template includes inZOI multi-language font, wheel/hover forwarding, close button.

tools.name: luamod_scaffold
tools.description:
Create a Lua mod or add lua/ scripts to an existing mod under the user InGame mods directory. TWO MODES:
  (A) NEW MOD: pass mod_name. Creates {mod_id}.uplugin, mod_manifest.json, lua/lua_manifest.json, lua/B2/Main.lua (global sim script), lua/B2/{script_name}.lua (per-character script), lua/B1/Main.lua (presentation script).
  (B) ADD TO EXISTING MOD: pass mod_id (must exist). Adds only the lua/ subtree to the existing mod. Useful for adding Lua scripts to a UI mod.
The generated per-target script is selected by 'type'/'key'/'env' (default: Zoi, key="*", B2). Its callback params carry LuaLS ---@param annotations (e.g. ---@param owner FB2Character) so hover/autocomplete works out of the box, and lua_manifest.json is written with the matching binding.
After scaffolding, use luamod_write_file to edit scripts and uimod_mount to load the mod in-game.
